Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself with a smaller version of the same problem. Each call does a tiny piece of the work and then hands the rest off to another call of itself, until it reaches a "base case" that can be answered directly without calling again. A classic example is factorial: `factorial(n)` returns `n * factorial(n-1)`, and stops when `n` reaches 1. The key idea is to trust that the smaller call will do its job correctly, just like trusting a loop to handle the earlier iterations.
